summary: A grid of covered cells, some hiding mines. Each move opens one covered cell: a mine ends the game; otherwise the cell shows how many of its eight neighbours hold mines, and a cell with none opens its neighbours in turn. The game is won when every cell without a mine is open.

cells.looks: a cell not yet opened, often drawn raised or in a colour of its own
an opened cell, flat, showing a digit from 1 to 8 whose colour follows the digit, or blank for 0
a covered cell with a mark on it, often a small flag
a mine drawn on a cell: the one opened, often on a red cell, and on some games every other once the game is lost
a cell hidden by an animation or a dialog

state_fields.grid: the grid's rows from the top, each a list of cells from the left: 0 to 8 an opened cell and the mines around it, 9 covered, 10 a covered cell marked with a flag, 11 a mine shown on a cell nobody opened, 12 the mine opened, null a cell nobody read (never the same as covered)
state_fields.score: always null: the game keeps no score
state_fields.scene: the id of the scene the screen shows

actions.description: one click or tap on a covered cell

scenes.looks: the grid with covered cells left to open
a notice that every safe cell is open, or the covered cells all marked
a notice that a mine was opened, or a mine shown on a red cell

meta_actions.description: start another game after the end, or instead of the one on the screen

mines.description: mines hidden on the grid, fewer than its cells; null when the screen does not say (the game is then played and judged by its numbers alone)

flags.description: whether moves place flags; only false is played: every move opens a cell, and a flag the game itself shows counts as a mine

first_open.description: what the first cell opened is promised: "around" (no mine on it nor on the cells around it) or "cell" (none on it alone); only the simulated game places its mines by it
